In Saints Row: The Third, players can participate in various activities, some of which were introduced in previous Saints Row games. These activities serve the plot, acting as training for the player-character or causing damage to the Syndicate. They can also be repeated outside of structured diversions.

The phrase "Mayhem, where players maximize property destruction before a time expires" is a description of one such activity. Some activities are based on two occasional poems published as broadsides and signed "M.M.", though the source texts have been lost. "To William Drummond of Hawthornden" is the title of Oxlie's dedicatory poem, which begins with formulaic humility: "I Never rested on the Muses bed, Nor dipt my Pen in the Helicon."

The Hanseatic League, or Hanse, was a commercial and defensive confederation of merchant guilds and market towns in Northwestern and Central Europe. It dominated maritime trade in the Baltic Sea and North Sea, especially in the late Middle Ages. The League was founded at Lübeck in 1356 and was most powerful in the late 15th century, when it included over 100 cities and towns. The Confederation did not receive much support from some Hanseatic cities at first, such as Bremen and Hamburg, which were exhausted due to previous wars and refused to provide any military support.
